{{also|fáce|facé|Face|FACE}}
==English==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|id=front part of the head|:inh|enm:face<id:front part of the head>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|face}}, from {{der|en|fro|face}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|facia}}, from {{der|en|la|faciēs||form, appearance}}. {{doublet|en|facies}}. Displaced native {{m|enm|onlete||face, countenance, appearance}}, {{m|enm|anleth||face}}, from {{noncog|ang|anwlite}}, {{m|ang|andwlita}}, compare {{noncog|de|Antlitz}}; {{noncog|ang|ansīen||face}}, {{noncog|enm|neb||face, nose}} (from {{noncog|ang|nebb}}), {{noncog|enm|leer|ler, leor, leer|face, cheek, countenance}} (from {{noncog|ang|hlēor}}), and non-native {{noncog|enm|vis||face, appearance, look}} (from {{noncog|fro|vis}}) and {{noncog|enm|chere|t=face}} from {{noncog|fro|chere}}.

In the sense of ''face'' as in reputation, influenced by {{semantic loan|en|zh|面子|notext=1}} or {{zh-l|臉}}, both of which mean literally the front of the head and metaphorically one's public image. See {{m|en|lose face}}.

===Etymology===
{{inh+|ro|la|facio|facere}}. The original past participle {{m|ro|fapt}} (< {{m+|la|factus}}) has been replaced by an analogical form. An alternative third-person simple perfect, ''fece'' (< {{m+|la|fēcit}}) was also found in some dialects.<ref>https://archive.org/details/grundrissderroma00gruoft</ref> The sense of “to cost” is likely a {{cal|ro|el|κάνω|nocap=1}}.
